body: TSMC's pure-foundry model (never competing with customers) plus relentless capex created a process lead once Intel's 10nm/7nm slipped (2016-20) and GlobalFoundries quit 7nm (2018). Apple A-series exclusivity (from ~A10, 2016, helped by InFO packaging) and then Nvidia/AMD AI accelerators (CoWoS advanced packaging) concentrated leading-edge demand on TSMC; gross margins >50%. ADR ~$15 in 2012 [unverified] -> record $319.61 (Jan 2026, $1.66tn) -> crossed $2tn market cap Feb 24 2026 -> record ~$363 (Apr 2026): ~24x plus dividends. Split: mostly EPS growth; P/E moved from ~12-15x to ~25-30x [approx]. Drawdown: ~-58% (Jan-Oct 2022) on cycle + Taiwan risk. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2017-19: Intel publicly delaying 10nm while TSMC shipped 7nm on schedule with Apple/AMD/Huawei; capex guidance rising faster than peers'; rising gross margin despite heavy depreciation. Who caught it / famous miss: Berkshire bought ~$4bn of ADRs in Q3 2022 near the low and sold almost all within a quarter, Buffett citing geopolitical risk [from memory, unverified in this pass]. LESSON: scale-driven manufacturing monopolies compound through cycles; the 'geopolitical discount' kept the P/E low for a decade and was itself the opportunity for those who could size for tail risk.

data.early_signals: Intel 10nm delays vs TSMC 7nm on time; Apple exclusivity; rising capex
data.lesson: manufacturing scale moat; geopolitical discount as opportunity, size for tail

title: TSMC 2012-2026: foundry scale + AI, ADR ~$15 -> $363, $2tn
